title: Knowledge Wiki employment context and hiring acceptance
objective: Make the governed public-safe Wiki useful for present-tense opportunity research and bounded portfolio acceptance testing without exposing private job-search context or giving simulated readers hidden evidence.

criteria.title: One authority and a private-source boundary
criteria.pass: Opportunity pages extend the canonical Knowledge Wiki; QA contexts do not duplicate claim or source authority; raw communications, warm paths, and application status remain outside Git.

criteria.title: Six current official opportunity contexts
criteria.pass: All six Tier 1 roles have official-employer URLs, live-state and freshness metadata, compensation and location facts, confirmed/inferred/unknown separation, and bounded one-year questions.

criteria.title: Stable requirements and honest coverage
criteria.pass: Requirement IDs are unique; proof and Wiki references resolve; visible, qualified, source-needed, experience-gap, hard-screen, and unknown states remain distinct.

criteria.title: Career and source-channel diagnostics
criteria.pass: Generated reports expose career-phase and source-channel coverage without treating equal density, private access, or source discovery as publication permission.

criteria.title: Title-blind discovery and negative controls
criteria.pass: The six known-good roles are recovered without titles; incompatible roles are rejected for credential, compensation, travel, or technical hard screens.

criteria.title: Hiring evaluator isolation
criteria.pass: The evaluator accepts only public route content plus public role and reader context; the Wiki gap resolver is a different operator and no evaluator packet contains hidden Wiki evidence.

criteria.title: Reader context integrity
criteria.pass: Generic and named reader contexts are configurable; every named profile has public sources, an explicit category, prohibited assumptions, and a simulation disclaimer.

criteria.title: Candidate and context binding
criteria.pass: Runtime packets record exact Git SHA, worktree state, public snapshot hash, opportunity hash, reader hash, suite hash, timestamp, and development or holdout panel identity.

criteria.title: Mutation resistance
criteria.pass: Tests reject private locators, stale roles, unsupported proof IDs, duplicate requirements, hidden hard screens, sole-authorship drift, private evaluator inputs, and unsourced named lenses.

criteria.title: Bounded public hill climb
criteria.pass: One small public change improves a decision-relevant signal using existing governed proof, adds no unsupported hiring claim, and leaves human hiring and application outcomes open.

human_gates.question: Does the exact public candidate remain true, warm, useful, and ready to use in an application?
Can the reader understand Jamie's category, strongest evidence, and honest limits without private coaching?
Does any later public projection require collaborator, rights, or consent review?
Was a real application submitted without this system delaying it by more than one working day?
